title: John Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 17.

questions.question: In John 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus prays for those given to him by the Father
Jesus says he has finished the work the Father gave him
Jesus asks the Father to glorify the Son
Jesus declares the hour has come
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus declares the hour has come
questions.explanation: John 17:1 states, 'These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come...'

questions.question: According to John 17:2, over what has the Father given Jesus power?
options: All flesh
All nations
All angels
All believers
questions.correctAnswer: All flesh
questions.explanation: John 17:2 says, 'As thou hast given him power over all flesh...'

questions.question: In John 17:3, what is described as eternal life?
options: To know the only true God and Jesus Christ
To have no pain or sorrow
To live forever on earth
To have many possessions
questions.correctAnswer: To know the only true God and Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: John 17:3 states, 'And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say he had finished according to John 17:4?
options: The work which the Father gave him to do
The journey to Jerusalem
The teaching of the disciples
Building the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The work which the Father gave him to do
questions.explanation: John 17:4 says, 'I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.'

questions.question: In John 17:5, Jesus asks the Father to glorify him with what?
options: The glory which he had with the Father before the world was
A crown of gold
The highest place in heaven
The angels of heaven
questions.correctAnswer: The glory which he had with the Father before the world was
questions.explanation: John 17:5 states, 'glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.'

questions.question: Who did Jesus say he had manifested God's name unto in John 17:6?
options: The men which the Father gave him out of the world
The Pharisees
The high priests
The Roman soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: The men which the Father gave him out of the world
questions.explanation: John 17:6 says, 'I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world.'

questions.question: According to John 17:7, what have the disciples known?
options: That all things given to Jesus are of the Father
That the world is evil
That Jesus will return soon
That the Father is silent
questions.correctAnswer: That all things given to Jesus are of the Father
questions.explanation: John 17:7 states, 'Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee.'

questions.question: What did Jesus give to the disciples according to John 17:8?
options: The words the Father gave him
Gold and silver
The keys to the kingdom
The law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The words the Father gave him
questions.explanation: John 17:8 says, 'For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them...'

questions.question: In John 17:8, what did the disciples believe about Jesus?
options: That he came out from the Father and was sent by Him
That he was a prophet only
That he was a carpenter
That he would never die
questions.correctAnswer: That he came out from the Father and was sent by Him
questions.explanation: John 17:8 states, '...they have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me.'

questions.question: According to John 17:9, for whom does Jesus pray?
options: For those given to him by the Father
For the whole world
For the rulers of the earth
For the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: For those given to him by the Father
questions.explanation: John 17:9 says, 'I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me.'

questions.question: According to John 17:1, to whom did Jesus lift up his eyes when he prayed?
options: Father
The disciples
The crowd
The heavens
questions.correctAnswer: Father
questions.explanation: John 17:1 states, 'These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father...'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said he prayed for the world in John 17.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17:9 states, 'I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said he glorified the Father on the earth according to John 17.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 17:4 says, 'I have glorified thee on the earth...'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said the disciples kept the Father's word in John 17.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: John 17:6 states, '...and they have kept thy word.'

questions.question: True or False: John 17 says Jesus asked for many riches and power on earth.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17 focuses on Jesus asking for glorification with the Father and praying for his disciples; it does not mention asking for riches or earthly power.

medium.title: John Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who is glorified in believers according to John 17:10?
options: The Son
The Father
The Holy Spirit
The believers
questions.correctAnswer: The Son
questions.explanation: Jesus states he is glorified in them, referring to the believers. (John 17:10)

questions.question: What does John 17:11 promise will happen if believers are kept through God's name?
options: They will be divided
They may be one, as we are
They will lose their faith
They will be taken out of the world
questions.correctAnswer: They may be one, as we are
questions.explanation: John 17:11 expresses Jesus' prayer for unity among believers, reflecting the unity between Him and the Father.

questions.question: According to John 17:12, who is referred to as the son of perdition?
options: Judas Iscariot
Peter
John
Matthew
questions.correctAnswer: Judas Iscariot
questions.explanation: The 'son of perdition' refers to Judas, who betrayed Jesus, indicating none were lost except him. (John 17:12)

questions.question: What is the purpose of Jesus speaking in the world according to John 17:13?
options: To condemn the world
That they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves
To gather more followers
To teach the law
questions.correctAnswer: That they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves
questions.explanation: John 17:13 indicates Jesus desires that His followers experience the fullness of His joy.

questions.question: According to John 17:14, why does the world hate believers?
options: Because they are rich
Because they are not of the world
Because they are weak
Because they are numerous
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are not of the world
questions.explanation: John 17:14 clarifies that believers are hated by the world because they do not belong to it, just as Jesus does not.

questions.question: What does Jesus pray for in John 17:15 regarding believers?
options: That they should be prosperous
That they should be taken out of the world
That they should be kept from the evil
That they should be punished
questions.correctAnswer: That they should be kept from the evil
questions.explanation: In John 17:15, Jesus requests that God protects His followers from evil while they remain in the world.

questions.question: According to John 17:16, believers are described as what?
options: Of the world
Not of the world
Lost
Confused
questions.correctAnswer: Not of the world
questions.explanation: John 17:16 emphasizes that believers, like Jesus, do not belong to the world.

questions.question: What does Jesus ask God to do in John 17:17?
options: To glorify Him
To sanctify them through thy truth
To take them away
To provide for them
questions.correctAnswer: To sanctify them through thy truth
questions.explanation: In John 17:17, Jesus requests sanctification for His followers, highlighting that God's word is truth.

questions.question: In John 17:18, how does Jesus relate His sending to the world to the sending of believers?
options: He sent them to judge the world
He sends them into the world as He was sent
He sends them to gather riches
He does not send them at all
questions.correctAnswer: He sends them into the world as He was sent
questions.explanation: John 17:18 states that just as the Father sent Jesus into the world, He also sends believers into the world.

questions.question: How does Jesus' prayer reflect His relationship with the Father according to John 17:1?
options: He is unrelated
He seeks glorification
He is angry
He feels abandoned
questions.correctAnswer: He seeks glorification
questions.explanation: In John 17:1, Jesus lifts His eyes to heaven, asking the Father to glorify Him, which reflects their close relationship.

questions.question: According to John 17:3, what is described as eternal life?
options: Knowing the Father and Jesus Christ
Being wealthy
Living forever
Following the law
questions.correctAnswer: Knowing the Father and Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent.

questions.question: What does John 17:4 indicate about Jesus' mission on earth?
options: He abandoned it
He finished the work given to Him
He failed
He was distracted
questions.correctAnswer: He finished the work given to Him
questions.explanation: In John 17:4, Jesus states that He has completed the work the Father appointed Him, affirming His obedience.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus prayed for the world in John 17:9.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17:9 clearly states that Jesus did not pray for the world but for those given to Him, emphasizing His focus on believers.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus asks God to take believers out of the world in John 17:15.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In John 17:15, Jesus prays for God to keep believers from evil, not to remove them from the world.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus manifests God's name to everyone in John 17:6.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17:6 specifies that Jesus manifested God's name to the men given to Him, not to everyone.

hard.title: John Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 17.

questions.question: According to John 17:19, why does Jesus sanctify himself?
options: That they also might be sanctified through the truth
To fulfill the law perfectly
To prepare for his resurrection
To demonstrate his divinity before the world
questions.correctAnswer: That they also might be sanctified through the truth
questions.explanation: John 17:19 states Jesus sanctifies himself 'that they also might be sanctified through the truth.'

questions.question: In John 17:20, for whom does Jesus pray besides those immediately with him?
options: Those who shall believe on me through their word
The rulers of the world
The people of Israel only
The angels in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Those who shall believe on me through their word
questions.explanation: John 17:20 specifies Jesus prays 'not for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word.'

questions.question: What is the purpose of the unity Jesus prays for in John 17:21?
options: That the world may believe that thou hast sent me
That the disciples may have power over all flesh
That the Jews may be delivered from Rome
That the temple may be rebuilt
questions.correctAnswer: That the world may believe that thou hast sent me
questions.explanation: John 17:21 says the unity is 'that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.'

questions.question: What has Jesus given to believers according to John 17:22?
options: The glory which thou gavest me
The law of Moses
The power to perform miracles
The earthly kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The glory which thou gavest me
questions.explanation: John 17:22 states Jesus has given them 'the glory which thou gavest me.'

questions.question: In John 17:24, what does Jesus desire for those given to him by the Father?
options: That they be with me where I am
That they receive great wealth
That they become rulers over Israel
That they fast and pray continually
questions.correctAnswer: That they be with me where I am
questions.explanation: John 17:24 expresses Jesus' will 'that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am.'

questions.question: According to John 17:26, what does Jesus declare to the believers?
options: Thy name, so that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them
The laws of the Old Testament
The mysteries of the kingdom of heaven
The coming destruction of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Thy name, so that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them
questions.explanation: John 17:26 says Jesus declared 'thy name, and will declare it: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'hagiazo' (ἁγιάζω) in John 17:19 mean?
options: To sanctify or set apart as holy
To judge or condemn
To teach or instruct
To heal or restore
questions.correctAnswer: To sanctify or set apart as holy
questions.explanation: 'Hagiazo' in John 17:19 means 'to sanctify or set apart as holy,' indicating Jesus sets himself apart for a holy purpose.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in John 17:21-23 to emphasize unity?
options: Chiasm
Parable
Metaphor
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: John 17:21-23 uses chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order, emphasizing unity between Father, Son, and believers.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine unity and love found in John 17:23?
options: Psalm 133:1 - 'Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!'
Genesis 1:1 - 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.'
Exodus 20:3 - 'Thou shalt have no other gods before me.'
Isaiah 53:5 - 'He was wounded for our transgressions.'
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 133:1 - 'Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!'
questions.explanation: Psalm 133:1 emphasizes unity among brethren, paralleling Jesus' prayer in John 17:23 for believers to be made perfect in one.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of eternal life through knowing God and Jesus as stated in John 17:3?
options: 1 John 5:20 - 'And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding.'
Romans 8:28 - 'All things work together for good.'
James 2:24 - 'Ye see then how that by works a man is justified.'
Revelation 21:4 - 'God shall wipe away all tears.'
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 5:20 - 'And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding.'
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:20 complements John 17:3 by affirming knowledge of the Son of God grants eternal life.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Jesus' prayer for sanctification of Himself in John 17:19?
options: John 17:18 - 'As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.'
John 17:20 - 'Neither pray I for these alone...'
John 17:17 - 'Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.'
John 17:21 - 'That they all may be one...'
questions.correctAnswer: John 17:18 - 'As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.'
questions.explanation: John 17:18 directly precedes verse 19 and shows Jesus sending disciples into the world, setting context for His sanctification.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'glory' in John 17:5 relate to Old Testament descriptions of God’s glory?
options: Both emphasize divine presence and majesty
The OT only associates glory with angels
The NT redefines glory as human achievement
Glory in OT is always physical brightness
questions.correctAnswer: Both emphasize divine presence and majesty
questions.explanation: John 17:5’s reference to glory aligns with OT themes (e.g., Exodus 33:18-23) where God's glory signifies divine presence and majesty.

questions.question: Which typology is reflected in Jesus' prayer for unity in John 17:21 as foreshadowing?
options: The unity of the Church as the Body of Christ
The division of Israel into two kingdoms
The exile and return from Babylon
The building of Solomon’s Temple
questions.correctAnswer: The unity of the Church as the Body of Christ
questions.explanation: John 17:21 foreshadows the Church’s unity as one body, a key New Testament typology linking believers with Christ and the Father.

questions.question: True or False: According to John 17:25, Jesus says the world has known the Father but those given to Him have not.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17:25 states, 'the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me,' so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: John 17:15 reveals Jesus prays for believers to be taken out of the world.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 17:15 says, 'I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil,' so Jesus does not pray for their removal.

theological.title: John Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 17:3 teach about eternal life?
options: Eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent
Eternal life is a future reward only after death
Eternal life depends on human works and obedience
Eternal life is solely a spiritual existence without relational knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent
questions.explanation: John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom God has sent, emphasizing relational knowledge rather than mere duration or works.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in John 17:17?
options: Sanctification is accomplished through God's truth, which is His word
Sanctification is a human effort independent of divine revelation
Sanctification is purely ceremonial and linked to ritual law
Sanctification is only positional, not progressive
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is accomplished through God's truth, which is His word
questions.explanation: John 17:17 states 'Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth,' highlighting that sanctification is a divine work accomplished through the truth of God's word.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine election and preservation is taught in John 17:12?
options: Jesus kept those given to Him by the Father, and none was lost except the son of perdition
Divine election is conditional and can be lost by any believer
Jesus did not keep any of those given to Him
Election is unrelated to preservation through Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus kept those given to Him by the Father, and none was lost except the son of perdition
questions.explanation: John 17:12 affirms that Jesus preserved all given to Him by the Father during His earthly ministry except the son of perdition, teaching the doctrine of divine election and preservation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 17:1 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Immutability
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: John 17:1 shows Jesus acknowledging the Father's sovereign authority to glorify the Son at the appointed hour, demonstrating God's sovereignty over salvation history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in John 17:24?
options: Eternal love
Wrath
Transcendence
Immanence
questions.correctAnswer: Eternal love
questions.explanation: John 17:24 speaks of the Father's love for the Son before the foundation of the world, highlighting the eternal and unchanging love within the Godhead.

questions.question: How does John 17:18 connect to the broader biblical theme of mission?
options: It extends Jesus' sending mission to His disciples, emphasizing continuation of divine mission
It rejects any mission for believers after Jesus' ascension
It limits the mission to Israel only
It focuses only on Jesus’ personal mission without involving others
questions.correctAnswer: It extends Jesus' sending mission to His disciples, emphasizing continuation of divine mission
questions.explanation: John 17:18 explicitly states Jesus sending His followers into the world as the Father sent Him, connecting to the biblical theme of missional continuity and obedience.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does John 17:20–21 highlight?
options: The unity of believers as a testimony to the world that Jesus was sent by the Father
The separation of the church from the world without witness
The futility of unity among believers
The church’s independence from the Father and Son
questions.correctAnswer: The unity of believers as a testimony to the world that Jesus was sent by the Father
questions.explanation: John 17:20–21 prays for believers’ unity 'that the world may believe that thou hast sent me,' showing the unity of the church as a redemptive sign to the world.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 17:9 and John 17:15 teach about Jesus' intercession?
options: Jesus prays specifically for His own given disciples, asking protection from evil but not removal from the world
Jesus prays for the entire world to be taken out of it
Jesus prays only for the world, not for His disciples
Jesus prays for His disciples to be exempt from trials by being removed from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus prays specifically for His own given disciples, asking protection from evil but not removal from the world
questions.explanation: John 17:9 shows Jesus praying specifically for those given to Him, and 17:15 clarifies He does not ask for their removal from the world but protection from evil.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 17:22 and John 17:23 teach about the nature of unity among believers?
options: Unity among believers is modeled on the unity between Father and Son and is empowered by sharing in divine glory
Unity is purely organizational without spiritual significance
Unity requires cultural uniformity rather than spiritual oneness
Unity is not essential for Christian witness
questions.correctAnswer: Unity among believers is modeled on the unity between Father and Son and is empowered by sharing in divine glory
questions.explanation: John 17:22–23 teach that believers’ unity mirrors the Father-Son unity and is grounded in the glory given by the Father to the Son, indicating a spiritual and divine basis for church unity.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do John 17:4 and John 17:19 provide about Jesus’ work and sanctification?
options: Jesus declares He finished the Father's work and sanctifies Himself for the sake of believers’ sanctification
Jesus claims to have failed the Father’s work and sanctification is left to believers alone
Jesus does not connect His work with sanctification
Sanctification is unrelated to Jesus’ mission on earth
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus declares He finished the Father's work and sanctifies Himself for the sake of believers’ sanctification
questions.explanation: John 17:4 states Jesus finished the work given by the Father, and 17:19 says He sanctifies Himself so believers may be sanctified, linking His mission to the believers’ holiness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim John 17:20–26 teaches that only the immediate disciples are to be united and loved. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Jesus prays not only for His immediate disciples but also for all who will believe through their word
Jesus prays exclusively for the twelve disciples and excludes future believers
The prayer is only a historical record with no application to future believers
The unity prayed for applies only to a select ethnic group
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus prays not only for His immediate disciples but also for all who will believe through their word
questions.explanation: John 17:20 clearly states Jesus prays 'neither for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word,' extending the prayer to all future believers.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine glory is taught in John 17:5?
options: Jesus asks to be glorified with the same glory He had with the Father before the world existed
Jesus denies having any glory before His earthly ministry
Divine glory is only given after resurrection
Glory is unrelated to Jesus’ pre-existence
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus asks to be glorified with the same glory He had with the Father before the world existed
questions.explanation: John 17:5 shows Jesus requesting to be glorified with the glory He shared with the Father before creation, affirming His pre-existent divine status and glory.

questions.question: What doctrine about the knowledge of God is taught in John 17:25?
options: Jesus knows the righteous Father, whereas the world does not know Him
The world has full knowledge of God’s righteousness
Knowledge of God is irrelevant to salvation
Both Jesus and the world have equal knowledge of the Father
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knows the righteous Father, whereas the world does not know Him
questions.explanation: John 17:25 contrasts the world's ignorance of the righteous Father with Jesus’ own knowledge and the knowledge given to His followers, highlighting the exclusivity of true divine knowledge.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 17:6 and John 17:8 teach about revelation and faith?
options: Jesus manifested the Father’s name to the disciples who received His words and believed He came from God
Revelation is only partial and does not lead to faith
Faith is independent from knowledge of the Father’s name
The disciples rejected Jesus’ words and did not believe
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus manifested the Father’s name to the disciples who received His words and believed He came from God
questions.explanation: John 17:6 states Jesus manifested the Father’s name to those given to Him, and 17:8 notes they received His words and believed He was sent by God, linking revelation with faith.

questions.question: What doctrine about believers' relationship to the world is taught in John 17:14 and John 17:16?
options: Believers are not of the world just as Jesus is not of the world, which explains the world's hatred
Believers fully belong to the world and should conform to it
Believers are to isolate completely from the world without any interaction
Believers and Jesus share the world's values and culture
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are not of the world just as Jesus is not of the world, which explains the world's hatred
questions.explanation: John 17:14 and 17:16 both affirm believers are 'not of the world' as Jesus is not, explaining why the world hates them, emphasizing their distinct spiritual identity.
